topic: the yubiOS mitigations document (docs/MITIGATE.md): the Faux Phy Qualcomm attack chain, each mitigation, why it is load-bearing, and the hardware bring-up discipline it records

subtopics.scope: The Faux Phy ... Phe Phum v1.05 Qualcomm supply-chain and absolute persistence attack chain itself: its three phases (OEM/vendor persistence, pre-init hijack, runtime control) and why every yubiOS defence rests on cryptographic validation before execution.

subtopics.scope: Step 1 mitigations for OEM/vendor persistence: modified power manager and stacked PME (PCR 4, signed UKI, ConditionSecurity=measured-os, bootctl enroll-keys, chipsec), stacked UEFI evil-twin EDK2 and broken CNTVOFF_EL2, and CVE/page-cache/hidden-GPT vectors (dm-verity, DPS UUID-only mount, RestrictFileSystems).
seed_queries: dirtyfrag page cache poisoning Linux attack

subtopics.scope: Step 2 mitigations before systemd init: obfuscated kernel modules (signed initrd in UKI, kernel lockdown, IMA, CoreSight disabled on arm64), modified libselinux/libapparmor and /usr bind-mount poison (dm-verity on every IO, usrhash=), poisoned generators, journal flushing and NVMe/GPT-auto blocking (PCR phase measurements, DPS fallback discovery).
seed_queries: systemd UKI initrd PE section PCR 11 measured boot

subtopics.scope: Step 3 runtime-control mitigations: faux ACPI tables blocked by signed cmdline, no TEE dependency (YubiKey FIDO2 instead of TrustZone), Computrace detection via chipsec, radio persistence and framebuffer password exfil (no typed passphrase, pam-u2f, PrivateNetwork=), and dmesg/proc scrubbing with fd hijacking (dm-verity service units, DynamicUser=, ProtectProc=invisible, NoNewPrivileges=, journal forward-secure sealing).

systemd journal forward sealing journalctl --verify FSS

subtopics.scope: Internal-record subtopic: the MITIGATE.md attack surface chart (21 surfaces mapped to controls with Block/Contain, Detect/Reduce, and architectural-immunity coverage classes) and the mermaid attack-flow graph tying each Step 1-3 stage to its mitigation.

What yubiOS cannot fully prevent: Computrace in UEFI ROM below the boot chain, hardware-wired radios that ignore OS power commands, novel dirtyfrag-class kernel CVEs, Qualcomm dload sideload running below the dm-verity Merkle tree, and a malicious UEFI supply chain root; the hardware-selection escape routes (open-firmware radios like Intel AX210, non-Qualcomm ARM64 boards in ADR-017).

subtopics.scope: The mitigation matrix's primary-threat table and threat model assumptions: owner vs attacker model, LUKS2 with FIDO2 hmac-secret (PIN, touch, offline recovery key), composefs over erofs with dm-verity and signed UKI cmdline, digest pins in PINNED.md with build policy and provenance/SBOM, owner-enrolled Secure Boot keys with PIV signing and sbverify in CI, avoidance of PCR-hash-bound LUKS unlock, pam-u2f local auth, per-user systemd-homed LUKS2 homes, and X25519MLKEM768 post-quantum TLS defaults.

subtopics.scope: The platform-specific risk split: ARM64 as primary platform (vendor secure-world ownership via TF-A + OP-TEE + fTPM, Path A/Path B board provisioning and sacrificial-board rehearsal, RPMB/fTPM NV bootstrap, U-Boot console break-in gate idea, CoreSight exposure, Qualcomm-style sideload avoidance) versus x86-64 as supported-but-secondary (OEM UEFI compromise, vendor TPM/fTPM ownership, VM CI false confidence).
